title: Surveillance Pricing May Be Coming to a Store Near You

summary:
What if the electronic shelf label you see at the grocery store isn't just showing you the price of the jar of mayonnaise you're about to buy — but actually raising the price because you put a can of tuna in your cart.

It's called surveillance pricing and retailers like Walmart appear to be locking down technology that will help them figure out how much they can charge you. title: Bloomberg Businessweek Daily: Gearing Up for Earnings (Podcast)
title_cn: Bloomberg Businessweek Daily: Gearing Up for Earnings (Podcast)
summary:
The people, companies and trends shaping the global economy. Watch Carol and Tim LIVE every day on YouTube: http://bit.ly/3vTiACF

Wall Street traders betting on another solid corporate earnings season sent stocks higher despite lingering concerns about still-elevated energy prices and bond yields. Brent crude fluctuated around $104, bringing little relief to investors worried about inflationary pressures that could make the Federal Reserve raise interest rates. Corporate America is now navigating one of the strongest profit cycles in recent history, with the S&P 500 posting seven consecutive quarters of double-digit earnings growth.

On today's episode:
Seth Fiegerman, Bloomberg News AI Editor
Logitech CEO Hanneke Faber
Robert Schiffman, Senior Tech Credit Analyst for Bloomberg Intelligence
Barbara Reinhard, CIO: Multi-Asset Strategies & Solutions at Voya Investment Management (Source: Bloomberg)
